parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, imprisonment, facility ban, custody placement, or border-document practice is documented for visitors; same-sex conduct is legal and motor issues are resident-facing, so LGR removal, marriage ban and age-25 care floor are not deducted as traveler exposure. Against that, police blackmail/extortion of LGBTQ people on dating/social media, high law-enforcement stigma, frequent discrimination/violence, MP calls to beat Pride participants, and hostile official/media climate show state-tolerated targeting and thin recourse if outed. Severity is major harassment/extortion/missed care rather than imprisonment/execution.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No border rejection or foreign-document doubting is shown.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. No X-marker or mismatch protocol is shown.
entry_documents.interaction: Resident LGR removal since 2021 does not itself affect a home passport; it is a climate signal only.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No visitor arrest, detention conditions, or birth-sex custody placement is sourced.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No custody protocol or consular-access practice shown.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Police extortion could escalate to detention, but no documented custody outcome is provided.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No bathroom, ward, shelter, or women-only-space rule for visitors is shown.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Not documented. No facilities protection is shown.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No combined national/local facility regime is documented; capital/rural difference beyond ostracism is unevidenced.

care_services.exposure: Access barriers for trans people regionally are documented, but no visitor-specific denial or medication seizure is shown.
care_services.protection: Not documented. No visitor care-continuity protection shown.
care_services.interaction: Resident age-25 floor and draft care ban (first reading only) do not establish visitor denial and are not counted as in-force exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented 2018 police blackmail of LGBTQ people for $70-$500 on dating/social media; 2023 vague child-protection expansion on promoting non-traditional relations; 2025 anti-LGBT pushes and MP transphobic campaign.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No non-discrimination statute is described; no documented traveler-facing remedy.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Vague expression terms plus police extortion increase outing/blackmail risk, but expired 2014 bill and unpassed 2026 draft are not in force.

minors_guardians.exposure: Uncertain. 2023 child-protection amendments are vague and do not mention orientation explicitly; no documented action against travelling families/minors.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented. No family-travel protection shown.
minors_guardians.interaction: Draft law affecting minors has passed only first reading, so it is not operative exposure for a guardian/minor visitor.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Frequent discrimination/violence against LGBTQ people, ~300% increase reported after 2014 reforms (dated), high stigma particularly from law enforcement, MP called for beating 2019 marchers.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Other MPs condemned the call; no documented prosecution, protection protocol, or remedy for victims is shown.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Hostile public/official framing plus police as perpetrators weakens the likelihood police would protect an outed visitor.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No traveler remedy, complaint outcome, or legal-aid route is documented; absence of evidence is not safety.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertain border, facilities, custody and care practices cannot be credited as protective; known police-hostility evidence carries weight over silence.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: police stops/interviews, extortion-type pressure and weak court recourse without imprisonment. Here blackmail is documented but routine visitor detention, fines and confiscation pattern is not, so slightly above 0.35.

Higher safety: national equality protection, release ordered by courts, apology/compensation after mismatch detention. Here no such protection or working remedy is documented and police are documented perpetrators, so materially below 0.65.

Lower safety: criminalised presentation, months in custody, beatings and capital provision. Here same-sex conduct is legal, no trans-specific imprisonment, custody abuse or execution pathway is documented, so well above 0.15.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: generally legal presence for same-sex conduct but documented police extortion, pervasive stigma/violence, hostile official framing and no described anti-discrimination recourse. Unknowns on borders, facilities, custody and care are not treated as safe, yet no universal-exposure rule or custodial harm is documented to place the case at 0.25 or below. If outed, the likely harms are blackmail, humiliation, discrimination and assault with limited protection, not imprisonment or death. That supports Elevated/High risk around 0.40.
